text:
There is a specific kind of chaos that ensues when a three-pound ball of fluff is convinced it is a guardian of the realm. My neighbor, in a fit of dramatic irony, put up a sign that read "Beware of Dog." It was meant to be a warning, but for my dog, Barnaby, it was a job offer.

The first time the postman arrived, Barnaby didn’t bark; he vibrated. He shot out the door like a fuzzy cannonball, his tiny legs a blur of panic and purpose. The postman, a man who has seen it all, looked down at the trembling speck of fur and deadpanned, "Oh no, I'm so scared!"

That was the moment Barnaby’s life changed. He didn’t just accept the insult; he internalized it. Now, every time the mail truck rumbles down the street, Barnaby launches himself into battle with the intensity of a lion defending its pride. He barks at shadows, he growls at squirrels, and he stares down the postman with the fierce determination of a creature who has something to prove.

The postman, meanwhile, has started bringing treats. Not because he’s afraid, but because he’s trying to bribe the tiny tyrant into a ceasefire. Barnaby, however, interprets the treats as tribute. He accepts them with a regal nod, then immediately returns to his post, guarding the house from the terrifying threat of... well, everything.

I tried to explain to him that he is, in fact, edible by most predators, but he just wagged his tail and barked at a leaf. Some missions are too important to question.
